title: Acacia Springs clinic workflow onramp notes
content:
Background:
- Clinic: Acacia Springs Community Health (regional outpatient network, 6 sites). Want a lightweight teletriage assistant + note summarization. Concern: PHI must remain in-customer VPC or on-prem; no hosted tokens allowed for clinical text.
- Engagement: pilot to run for 3 months, one site first (Main St.), then roll to others. Primary contact: Dr. Luis Moreno (IT lead: Hannah Kim).

Attendees (initial kickoff 2024-11-15):
- Priya Kapoor (Redwood CS)
- Samir Patel (Redwood Solutions Eng)
- Dr. Luis Moreno (Acacia IT/Clinical)
- Hannah Kim (Acacia IT)
- Jana Müller (Redwood PM, notes)

High-level ask:
- Real-time teletriage assistant in clinic EHR UI (sidebar).
- Summarize visit notes into templated SOAP-like structure.
- Redaction / PII detection pre-send to model.
- SLA: 500ms-1s median latency for small summarization calls (<=512 tokens) in primary site.

Key constraints / non-negotiables:
- All inference must run inside their AWS account (VPC) or on-prem.
- KMS/HSM keys for data encryption; customer manages keys.
- Audit logs retained for 365 days, must be accessible to their compliance team.
- No external model telemetry leaving account; Redwood private control plane OK if configured with no PHI exports.

Initial technical notes / gotchas observed during call:
- Acacia runs Epic-light EHR with a custom iframe-based sidebar. Sidebar communicates via gateway within VPC — we need to validate CORS and routing for streaming SSE.
- Their busiest windows have short bursts (11:30-13:00) where dozens of nurses may do summaries. Need autoscaling strategy + warm pools.
- Concern about cold-start latency for quantized models on smaller GPUs. Recommend dedicated warm pool for Main St. (min-cap 2 instances).
- Their network uses strict egress filtering; our private agent will need explicit egress rules for package updates. Ops were worried about outbound ports during maintenance windows.

Model / runtime considerations:
- Use a compact instruction-following model (quantized 4-bit) with local KV cache for quick turnarounds.
- Suggest Redwood Private (VPC) deployment with pinned model version. Fallback rule: small hosted replica only for non-PHI metadata if customer allows (they currently do not).
- Need to prebuild prompt templates for SOAP mapping; keep prompt size small, rely on structured extraction.

Privacy / compliance action items:
- Redaction layer: run local preprocessor (regex + ML PII detector) before any tokens hit the model. Determine whether last-4 SSN or MRN patterns must be masked.
- Audit schema: event-level logs (request id, model id, non-PHI hashes) must be stored in s3 bucket (customer). Provide log format sample.
- KMS integration: verify CMKs can be used by Redwood Private components; get IAM principals list.

Open questions (needs research / follow-up):
- Q1: Can Acacia accept streaming SSE inside their iframe? (Hannah to confirm with front-end team)
- Q2: How many concurrent summarization requests during peak? (They estimated 20-30, but need real metrics for autoscaling)
- Q3: Acceptance of 4-bit quantized model quality for clinical summaries? (Clinical leads to review examples)
- Q4: Retention window for temp KV cache — compliance asked for auto-eviction after 5 minutes, confirm acceptable.

Low-level integration gotchas to prototype:
- EHR sidebar auth: token refresh cadence is 10 minutes; avoid long-lived model sessions tied to user tokens — use short-lived session mapping in Redwood gateway.
- If we use prefix cache keyed by patient-id + template-id, need to ensure no accidental cross-patient leakage (namespace must include site + encounter id + hash of template).
- Their load balancer strips certain headers by default; may need to inject X-Forwarded-For mapping in the agent.

Proposed minimal viable pilot (MVP):
- Deploy Redwood Private in Acacia AWS account (single region us-east-1) 
- Warm pool: 2 ded. GPU instances running quantized model (gpus: T4x or A10x) 
- Feature set: in-iframe summarization (sync, <=512 tokens), redaction preprocessor, audit logs to their s3, KMS-wrapped model cache
- Success criteria (30-day): median latency <= 1s; 80% clinician satisfaction on summary quality; zero PHI exfiltration incidents.

Action items / owners:
- Samir: draft infra diagram + IAM principals list needed for CMK access (due 2024-11-27) -> LINK: GH PR stub attached (see linked artifacts)
- Hannah: confirm iframe SSE support and LB header behavior (due 2024-11-22)
- Dr. Moreno: provide 10 de-identified sample notes for prompt tuning and QA (due 2024-12-02)
- Jana: prepare clinical acceptance rubric (example templates + edge cases) (due 2024-11-29)
- Priya (me): assemble pilot SOW draft and rough cost estimate for dedicated warm pool (due 2024-11-25)

Risks / mitigations:
- Performance risk on small GPUs: mitigate by capacity buffer + use of KV cache and batching within site windows.
- Compliance risk if redaction fails: mitigation = mandatory local redaction + manual QA sampling for first 1000 summaries.
- Ops risk on patch windows: schedule maintenance off-peak and ensure image update process respects egress rules.

Notes to self (quick):
- Keep prompt tokens minimal; use structured JSON output so EHR can render fields directly.
- Follow up on CS-1894 for billing/discount clause for pilot.
- Check whether their s3 lifecycle policy will auto-delete logs (we want 365d).

Meeting follow-up plan:
- Weekly syncs (30m) for first 6 weeks: Tue 10:00 PT. Agenda: infra blockers, sample review, latency reports.
- Shared drive folder: create Acacia/Onramp/Artifacts and drop sample logs + prompt drafts (ask Hannah for s3 write access).

Quick copy of prompt prototype (example):
- Input: raw clinician note (up to 2k chars)
- System instructions: "Extract brief SOAP summary. Output JSON with keys: subject, objective, assessment, plan. Abbreviate to one sentence per section. Remove all PHI. If uncertain, add RA (requires-attention) tag."

End of file — will iterate after Hannah and Samir return answers.

-- Priya
